info.step1.title: Define the thread
info.step1.body: Select material, thread profile, thread size, thread length and safety distance.
info.step2.title: Select the thread mill
info.step2.body: Use a suggested SmiCut tool or enter custom tool dimensions in the tool selection.
info.step3.title: Check output
info.step3.body: Review cutting data, machining time and the Fanuc CNC program before machining.
info.beforeMachining.title: Before machining
info.beforeMachining.body: Check that the selected thread mill can machine the thread diameter, pitch and thread length. Confirm the program in simulation or single block before running production.
info.figureAlt: Thread milling dimension reference showing thread diameter, pitch, cutting length, safety distance and cutter diameter.
info.toolCompensation.title: Tool Compensation
info.toolCompensation.body: Compensation of tooling is normally only needed for small adjustments. Large compensation values can cause problems. Use a value close to zero for cutter diameter compensation in the control system tool library.
info.correctThreadDiameter.title: Correct Thread Diameter
info.correctThreadDiameter.body: The pitch diameter is usually checked with a thread plug gauge or another accepted thread measuring method. If adjustment is needed, compensate in the machine control rather than changing standard thread data.
info.customTools.title: Custom and Special Tools
info.customTools.body: If your tool is not in the list, choose custom tool dimensions in the tool selection and enter cutter diameter, cutting length and number of flutes. Verify the generated program carefully when using custom tooling.
info.threadBurr.title: ThreadBurr
info.threadBurr.body: To use the deburring feature of solid carbide thread mills from SmiCut, input the complete cutting length of the tool in the thread length box. That way the threading and deburring will be made in the same operation.
info.threadBurr.link: ThreadBurr – Solid Carbide Thread Mills from SmiCut
info.oneTwoRows.title: Thread Mills with One or Two Rows of Teeth
info.oneTwoRows.body: SmiProg compensates for standard SmiCut cutters with one or two rows of teeth. When using a non-standard cutter, check the cutting length and pitch relationship before machining.
info.flankInfeed.title: Flank Infeed
info.flankInfeed.body: SmiProg uses flank infeed when programming multiple radial passes. This helps reduce vibration and improves machining stability.
info.flankInfeed.link: Vibration-Free Thread Milling: Improving Productivity and Economy
info.shortCuttingLength.title: Short Cutting Length
info.shortCuttingLength.body: If the selected tool has a shorter cutting length than the requested thread length, SmiProg divides the operation into several axial passes when the tool type supports it.
info.inserts.title: Thread Mills with Inserts
info.inserts.body: Use custom tool dimensions in the tool selection to get cutting data for indexable thread mills. Enter the actual cutter diameter, cutting length and number of inserts or flutes, then verify the generated program before machining.
info.taperedThreads.title: Tapered Threads
info.taperedThreads.body: For tapered threads, the cutter diameter is related to the last full thread closest to the shank. Register the thread diameter at that position for correct CNC output.
info.warning.title: Warning
info.warning.body: The cutting data in SmiProg is recommended starting data. Many factors can require adjustments, including workpiece material, machine stability, fixturing, tool setup, coolant and chip evacuation. SmiCut does not take responsibility for damage caused by using the CNC program or cutting data recommended by the software.
